description:
DONE s457aj (Opus agent AJ, round 14).  Found by grouping the perl-t half of
the drop census by MECHANISM: the last two `Bug. Fell through. Missing case: []`
rows -- t/io/open.t:267 and t/op/utf8cache.t:70 -- were ONE mechanism, and the
EMPTY missing case was the tell (the reducer had been handed an operator with
no left operand and spliced the run down to nothing).

PERL'S RULE (probed 5.40.3, twelve spellings):

    sub f { $_[0] }
    f 5, || 7      # (f 5,) || 7   -> 5
    f 5, && 7      # (f 5,) && 7   -> 7
    f 5, . 7       # (f 5) . 7     -> "57"
    f 5, == 5      # (f 5) == 5    -> 1
    f 5, ? 1 : 2   # (f 5) ? 1 : 2 -> 1
    f "ab", =~ /a/ #               -> 1
    substr $x, 0, 1, = "Z"         # (substr $x,0,1,) = "Z"  -> lvalue substr
    f 5, - 7       # -7 is an ARGUMENT (unary minus): "5 -7"
    f 5, // 7      # perl SYNTAX ERROR (ambiguous with a regex)
    f 5, x 3       # perl SYNTAX ERROR
    print("a"), || print("b")      # perl SYNTAX ERROR -- the rule is the
                                   # paren-LESS list-operator run only

So: a list operator's argument list may end in a comma, and an operator that
CANNOT BEGIN A TERM then applies to the CALL, not to an argument.

FIX (one place, `Pl::PExpr::_listop_arg_ceiling` -- the #343/B2 boundary both
spellings already share): inside the ceiling scan, a token that is a
binary-only operator and whose predecessor in the run is `,` or `=>` ends the
run at that comma.  The trailing comma itself stays in the run and
`parse_list` already skips the empty part it produces ("Skip empty parts (can
happen with leading commas)").  The separators are excluded explicitly --
`f(1,,2)` is `f(1,2)` in perl, an empty MIDDLE slot, not a boundary.

RULE 11: "can this operator only be binary" existed as an inline
`%can_be_unary_op` hash + cast test + filetest regex inside handle_subcalls'
bareword classifier.  Extracted as `Pl::PExpr::_is_binary_only_op` and asked
by BOTH sites; nothing else in the tree spells that class.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 + shapes; emission A/B vs a 0237940
worktree over 923 files (lib 23 + perl t/ 605 + cpan-tests t/ 289 + shapes)
= exactly these two files DIFF, 0 RCDIFF; gate-SET scan over BOTH populations
(638x2) = exactly two verdict moves, both drop -> OK.

CENSUS: 21 files / 65 drops -> 19 / 63 (rows edited out by hand with cause).
SUITE (spliced into baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv with cause):
  t/op/utf8cache.t  DIFF 14/0 -> OK 16/0   FULLY PASSING
  t/io/open.t       DIFF 142/23 -> 153/35  -- the drop was aborting the
      enclosing form, so the file produced 165 rows where perl produces 188;
      it now runs to the end.  +11 pass, +12 honest fails, every one of them a
      row that had never run (embedded-NUL pathnames, warnings-gated
      diagnostics, scalar-handle buffering).  New sig `unbound:$99` = task #851.

GUARD: Pl/t/listop-ceiling-01.t rows 6 (positive, six operator spellings) and
7 (the inverses: `- 7` is an argument, `2 . "x"` stays in the run, `f(1,,2)`,
a parenthesised trailing comma).  Inverse-run on a 0237940 worktree: row 6
fails there, row 7 passes there and here -- it is a pure inverse.
subject: A paren-less list operator's argument list may END IN A COMMA -- `substr $x,0,1, = "Z"` and `ok f(),'d',\n|| _diag $!` swallowed the operator into the run and DROPPED the whole statement
